lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Welcome to Outpost Gale, Commander {name}! I'm BOLT, the base robot. I explain things. You make the calls.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: I'm Mira, the botanist. My job is food, so I worry about food.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Tomas, geologist. We came to Mars for science, Commander!

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: A [[sol]] is one Mars day. The next crew lands after the last sol, and our job is to get the base ready for them.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Three meters keep us alive: Power, Life Support and Crew Health. Every action spends daylight hours, and you get 8 each sol.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Click a room to walk there and use it. Try the Airlock: go to the crater rim and bring back some [[regolith]].

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Outside, the crew takes a [[dose|radiation dose]]. The farther you go, the better the haul, and the bigger the dose.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Living off what we find on Mars has a name: [[isru|ISRU]]. Every rock counts!

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Nice build! Every upgrade helps one meter and costs something else. No choice is free.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: New machines switch on at the start of the next sol.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: An air leak! Fix it now, or let it drain Life Support every night. Both are allowed. It's your call.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Dust all over the panels. We're on half power until someone goes out and wipes them.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: The plants look sick! The greenhouse won't make food until I treat them.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: The water recycler is jammed. Machines on Mars break, just like on the space station.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Outpost Gale, a cargo pod landed near you. Grab the spare parts within 2 sols.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Everyone's exhausted. We've been working non-stop. A rest in the hab would help.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Fun fact: real radio messages take about 4 to 24 minutes between Earth and Mars. In this game, Earth's news is always one sol late.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Earth watches the Sun for [[flare|flares]]. A flare is a warning sign. The fast particles that can follow are the danger.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Outpost Gale, that was a solar particle event, an [[sep|SEP]]. They often come after a big flare or a [[cme|CME]].

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Every storm in this game really happened. Check the storm card to see the date.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Tip: use the Radio, then decide about sealing the Storm Shelter.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Radiation [[dose]] adds up. Rest can't undo it, so the crew's max health just went down for the rest of the mission.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: A sealed Storm Shelter keeps the dose small. That's the trade: some power tonight for health that lasts.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Act 2: Dust Season. Dust storms will cut solar power for days at a time.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: Big battery or more panels? Mission Control just sent a battery blueprint.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Whatever we pick, keep the greenhouse lamps on!

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: See that haze on the horizon? Dust season is here. Keep some power in reserve.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Act 3: Solar Maximum. The Sun is busy, and Earth's warnings still come a sol late.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Commander {name}, we sent you a landing pad blueprint. The next crew can't land safely without one.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: Tomas looks worn out. Let's not overdo it.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Outpost Gale, the next crew's landing window is set. A big storm may arrive with it.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Everything at once now. There's no perfect answer, just good choices.

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: Power hit zero! The machines stopped and Life Support dropped. Try to keep a buffer.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: That rock sample unlocked a greenhouse blueprint! Fresh food, but the lamps need power.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: A water recycler blueprint! Less water to worry about, as long as it doesn't jam.

lines.speaker: mira
lines.text: A gym corner! Mars gravity is only about a third of Earth's, so our bones and muscles need exercise.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: With a bigger dish you'll hear our warnings sooner. Light speed doesn't change, though!

lines.speaker: bolt
lines.text: A wall segment only shields the room it touches. Cover the Hab and the Shelter for the full effect.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: We see the landing pad from orbit. Great work, Outpost Gale!

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Touchdown! The next crew is safe on the pad, and they say your base feels like home.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Touchdown on your pad! It was close, but you made it.

lines.speaker: tomas
lines.text: No pad yet, so the next crew lands out on the plain. Everyone's safe, though.

lines.speaker: earth
lines.text: Outpost Gale, we're bringing you home early. Everyone's safe. That's what matters.

terms.explain: One day on Mars. It lasts 24 hours and 39 minutes.
Loose Mars soil and dust. Piled up, it makes a good radiation shield.
How much radiation a body soaks up. Mars has a thin atmosphere and no magnetic shield, so the dose is higher than on Earth.
In-situ resource utilization: using what you find on Mars (soil, ice, air) instead of shipping everything from Earth.
A sudden flash of light and X-rays from the Sun. It's a warning sign that particles might follow.
Solar energetic particles: a burst of fast particles from the Sun. These are what give astronauts a big radiation dose.
Coronal mass ejection: a huge cloud of gas the Sun throws into space. It can push particles ahead of it.

endings.title: Thriving Outpost
endings.message: The next crew walks into a real home.
endings.tip: Try Commander mode, or a stormier season.
endings.parallel: NASA plans missions so each one prepares the way for the next, just like you did.

endings.title: Ready, Just Barely
endings.message: It was close, but you made it.
endings.tip: Keep every meter at 50 or more and build at least 3 upgrades besides the pad.
endings.parallel: The International Space Station was built up one mission at a time, starting in 1998.

endings.title: Holding On
endings.message: Everyone's safe. The next crew has work to do.
endings.tip: The landing pad blueprint arrives in Act 3. Save 8 regolith for it.
endings.parallel: Curiosity has explored Gale crater since 2012, one careful sol at a time.

endings.title: Early Ride Home
endings.message: The crew is evacuated. Here's what happened, and what to try next time.
endings.tip: Build something that refills your weakest meter early, and use the Radio before deciding about the shelter.
endings.parallel: In 2018 a planet-wide dust storm covered the Opportunity rover's solar panels. Its mission ended after almost 15 years.
